title: Hom objects from the standard simplex and its boundary are the term and the matching object
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $K$ a simplicial object of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, with matching objects $M_n(K)$, canonical morphisms $\mu_n:K_n\to M_n(K)$ (components $d_0,\dots,d_n$) and, for $n\geq1$, projections $\mathrm{pr}_i:M_n(K)\to K_{n-1}$ onto the $i$-th factor ($0\leq i\leq n$) [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. For $n\geq0$ let $\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial set with $\Delta[n]_m$ the set of order-preserving maps $\varphi:\lbrack m\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$ and $\Delta[n](\psi)(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\psi$, and let $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ be the simplicial subset whose $m$-simplices are the non-surjective $\varphi:\lbrack m\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$ (so $\partial\Delta[0]$ is empty). For $0\leq i\leq n$ let $\delta_i:\lbrack n-1\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$ be the injection omitting $i$, an $(n-1)$-simplex of $\partial\Delta[n]$. Then: (a) $\Delta[n]_m$ is finite and nonempty for all $m$ and $\Delta[n]$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices (the injective $\varphi$), and $K_n$ with the family $(K(\varphi):K_n\to K_m)_{\varphi\in\Delta[n]_m}$ is $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta[n],K)_0$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object]: this family is a $\Delta[n]$-family over $K_n$ and every $\Delta[n]$-family $(f_\varphi)$ over an object $W$ is $(K(\varphi)\circ f_{\mathrm{id}_{[n]}})_\varphi$ for the unique morphism $f_{\mathrm{id}_{[n]}}:W\to K_n$. (b) For $n\geq1$, $\partial\Delta[n]_m$ is finite and nonempty for all $m$ and $\partial\Delta[n]$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices, and there is a unique isomorphism $\theta:\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0\to M_n(K)$ with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\theta=u_{\delta_i}$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, where $(u_s)$ is the universal $\partial\Delta[n]$-family. (c) For $n\geq1$, if $\rho:K_n\to\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0$ is the unique morphism with $u_\varphi\circ\rho=K(\varphi)$ for every simplex $\varphi$ of $\partial\Delta[n]$ (the restriction morphism along $\partial\Delta[n]\subseteq\Delta[n]$ under the identification (a)), then $\theta\circ\rho=\mu_n$.

proof.text: For fixed m and n, the set of order-preserving maps $\lbrack m\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$ is finite (it is determined by the finite nondecreasing sequence of $m+1$ values in $\lbrack n\rbrack$) and is nonempty (for example, a constant map). A map is nondegenerate in the standard simplex exactly when it is injective: a noninjective nondecreasing map factors through a proper surjection $\lbrack m\rbrack\to\lbrack r\rbrack$ and hence is a degeneracy, while an injective map cannot factor through a set of smaller cardinality. There are only finitely many injective maps between the finite ordered sets $\lbrack m\rbrack$ and $\lbrack n\rbrack$, and no injective map exists for $m>n$, so $\Delta[n]$ has finitely many nondegenerate simplices. If $n\geq1$, the boundary consists of a subset of these finite sets and is nonempty in every degree because a constant map $\lbrack m\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$ is non-surjective; its nondegenerate simplices are the injective non-surjective maps, again a finite set. The empty boundary in degree $n=0$ is immediate since every map to $\lbrack0\rbrack$ is surjective.

source.place: Definition 0175 (definition-terminology-simplicial-sets) and Lemma 0177 (lemma-simplex-map), finiteness and nondegenerate simplices of the representable simplex and its boundary

proof.text: For part (a), let $W$ be an object of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$. The maps $K(\varphi):K_n\to K_m$ indexed by $\varphi\in\Delta[n]_m$ form a $\Delta[n]$-family because $K$ is contravariant: for $\psi:\lbrack l\rbrack\to\lbrack m\rbrack$, $K(\psi)$ composed with $K(\varphi)$ equals $K(\varphi\circ\psi)$, which is the component indexed by $\Delta[n](\psi)(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\psi$. Given any $\Delta[n]$-family $(f_\varphi)$ over $W$, take $g=f_{\mathrm{id}_{[n]}}$. The family relation for the simplex $\mathrm{id}_{[n]}$ gives $f_\varphi=K(\varphi)\circ g$, so $g$ is the only morphism producing the family. Conversely, for any $g:W\to K_n$, the family $(K(\varphi)\circ g)_\varphi$ satisfies the same relations by functoriality. The universal property in def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object therefore identifies $K_n$, with this family, with $\operatorname{Hom}(\Delta[n],K)_0$.

source.place: Lemma 0177 (lemma-simplex-map), proof: evaluation of a map on the identity simplex

proof.text: For $n\geq1$, boundary families are naturally the same as compatible tuples of codimension-one faces. Restriction sends a boundary family $(f_\varphi)$ to $x_i=f_{\delta_i}$. Conversely, let $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ satisfy $d_{j-1}\circ x_i=d_i\circ x_j$ for $i<j$. For a non-surjective $\varphi:\lbrack m\rbrack\to\lbrack n\rbrack$, choose $i$ outside its image and use lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-factorization to write $\varphi=\delta_i\circ\psi$; define $f_\varphi=K(\psi)\circ x_i$. If $i<j$ are two omitted values, then $j-1$ is omitted from the image of $\psi$, so factor $\psi=\delta_{j-1}\circ\xi$. The face identity of lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity gives $\delta_i\circ\delta_{j-1}=\delta_j\circ\delta_i$, and the tuple relation gives $K(\psi)\circ x_i=K(\delta_i\circ\xi)\circ x_j$, so $f_\varphi$ is independent of the omitted value. Functoriality of $K$ gives $K(\alpha)\circ f_\varphi=f_{\varphi\circ\alpha}$ for every $\alpha$, hence these maps form a boundary family. The two constructions are inverse (use $\delta_i=\delta_i\circ\mathrm{id}$ for the codimension-one components) and commute with precomposition in $W$. The tuple is therefore identified with the morphism to $M_n(K)$ by lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object (2), equivalently by the compatible-face description of lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces (1).

source.place: Lemma 018V (lemma-cosk-shriek), proof via Lemma 0186 (lemma-formula-limit), with the factorization and face relations from Lemmas 0166-0167

proof.text: Let $(u_\varphi)$ be the universal boundary family. Its codimension-one components $u_{\delta_i}$ satisfy the matching relations, so the universal property in lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object gives a unique morphism $\theta:\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0\to M_n(K)$ with $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\theta=u_{\delta_i}$. Conversely, apply the boundary-family construction of the preceding step to the tuple $(\mathrm{pr}_i)$ on $M_n(K)$; the representing property of $\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0$ gives a morphism $\eta:M_n(K)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0$. The composite $\theta\circ\eta$ has all projections $\mathrm{pr}_i$, hence is the identity by the matching-object universal property. The composite $\eta\circ\theta$ has the same universal boundary family as the identity, because both have the same $\delta_i$-components and the extension from codimension-one components is unique; it is therefore the identity by the universal property of $\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0$. Thus $\theta$ is the unique isomorphism claimed in (b), and its projection equations hold by construction.

source.place: Lemma 018V (lemma-cosk-shriek), proof: the boundary Hom object is the degree-n matching object

proof.text: For (c), the maps $K(\varphi):K_n\to K_m$ for boundary simplices form a boundary family, so def-weil-pbc-simplicial-hom-object gives the unique restriction morphism $\rho:K_n\to\operatorname{Hom}(\partial\Delta[n],K)_0$ with $u_\varphi\circ\rho=K(\varphi)$. For each $i$, $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\theta\circ\rho=u_{\delta_i}\circ\rho=K(\delta_i)=d_i$, while $\mathrm{pr}_i\circ\mu_n=d_i$ by the definition of the matching morphism. The matching-object universal property therefore forces $\theta\circ\rho=\mu_n$.

split_report.summary: Read Stacks simplicial.tex Lemmas 0177, 018V and 0186, including the proofs and the face factorization and face relation lemmas 0166-0167. No Lean declaration with this statement exists in WeilConjectures or Comparator. The split writes the finite/nonempty and nondegenerate-simplex checks, proves Hom(Delta[n], K)_0 = K_n by evaluation at the identity simplex, extends compatible codimension-one boundary faces to all non-surjective maps using the existing factorization and face-identity leaves, identifies the resulting functor with the matching object using lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-matching-object and lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces, and checks that the restriction map is the matching morphism. No new node was needed because every auxiliary statement is already present in the DAG or is proved explicitly inside a step.
